caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Best Buy Co., Inc.
court: USDC E.D. Cal. — Sacramento Division (proposed diversity filing)
claims: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E)/(j)(4)(A) — diversity-first v3; FCRA/ICRAA reserved after limitations audit
status: FEDERAL REDRAFT v3 — Best Buy opening complaint pivoted to diversity + §290.46 only. FCRA/ICRAA removed/reserved because the current May 29 legal-awareness chronology is not a sufficient top-tier factual discovery theory.
note: Current source of truth is PR #799 v4 complaint. Opening complaint is diversity + §290.46. FCRA/ICRAA stay off: Best Buy named First Advantage on October 17, 2023, and there is no truthful later discovery date. File the Penal Code count before Oct. 17, 2026. Do not name Lerma in the pleading. Do not plead arbitration/unconscionability. No REVIEW DRAFT banner on the caption. Contract/estoppel remain reserved.
defendants: Best Buy Co., Inc., a Minnesota corporation with its principal place of business in Richfield, Minnesota, is the proposed sole opening defendant as employer/user of the report. First Advantage Background Services Corp. is pleaded as Best Buy's CRA from Best Buy's own October 17, 2023 emails; it remains a nonparty discovery source unless Best Buy-specific records support an independent CRA claim. Jose Tapia (GM) and Daisy Calvary are witnesses. Best Buy Stores, L.P. is reserved if the personnel file shows a different employing affiliate.
causes: [OPENING FEDERAL CLAIM] Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E), (j)(4)(A) — Best Buy transaction documents identify First Advantage; registry source/use remain I&B; Plaintiff does not possess Best Buy's report and does not allege source-field wording as known fact.
[RESERVED] FCRA §1681b(b)(3)(A) — do not plead unless actual/constructive-discovery chronology supports timeliness under §1681p.
[RESERVED] ICRAA §§1786.40/1786.50 — do not plead unless factual discovery chronology supports §1786.52 timeliness.
[RESERVED] Written-contract / promissory-estoppel theories — not facially discarded under CCP §335.1; require offer-term, at-will, reliance, and arbitration audit before addition.
[OMITTED OPENING] UCL, CCRAA, Tameny/IIED, Fair Chance Act/FEHA, FCRA §1681m(a), First Advantage as defendant.
key_facts: On Oct. 13, 2023, Best Buy emailed that it had received Plaintiff's application for General Warehouse Worker / 2nd Shift at $22.60, requisition 928556BR. The warehouse is 6653 Hopkins Road, Tracy, CA 95377. On Oct. 17 at 3:47 p.m., Jose Tapia, General Manager, emailed a congratulations offer and required, within 24 hours, Candidate Zone signature, background-check information, and background-check authorization. At 4:22 p.m. Best Buy sent a background-authorization confirmation naming First Advantage Consumer Center. At 4:30 p.m. First Advantage ordered a Best Buy drug test (Q09078711; account BEST BUY 11759586; Quest Modesto is a collection option, not the worksite). Plaintiff accepted the offer and completed the drug screening. On information and belief, that screen came back clean. Best Buy then ceased communication and ghosted him. No pre-adverse letter, adverse letter, or Best Buy report is in the file. Report contents and use are I&B ultimate facts. Supporting basis: written offer, named First Advantage, same-day screen, contemporaneous Megan's Law listing, UPS/FedEx same-consumer comparators, no other basis communicated, and exclusive control of the Best Buy report.
procedural_status: Pre-filing federal v3 on PR #799. Diversity-first §290.46 complaint is current review pleading. Serve First Advantage inspection and Best Buy personnel-file demands; obtain arbitration policy; file before Oct. 17, 2026 if proceeding under §338(a).
damages: Opening federal draft seeks lost employment compensation at the offered $22.60 hourly rate according to proof and Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) remedies. The offer does not state weekly hours or a start date; those figures are not invented. Do not use FCRA/ICRAA or the optional civil penalty to establish AIC.
risk: Primary merits risk is source/use: actual Best Buy FADV report is not in the file. Lerma controls if the transaction-specific report contradicts registry sourcing; Donaleski permits independently sourced conviction information. Limitations: §290 remedial theory uses CCP §338(a) with current working outside date Oct. 17, 2026; do not rely on optional civil penalty. FCRA/ICRAA have serious constructive-discovery exposure because Best Buy named FADV and required BGC authorization in Oct. 2023; May 29, 2026 legal-theory awareness is retired as an opening pleading theory. Arbitration policy referenced in application must be obtained. Entity Best Buy Co., Inc. remains a filing gate.
